gaps.remediation: Keep the published incident response plan and supported versions policy current. Record a product response exercise and evidence of advisory and notification procedures. Your organization approves, exercises, and records its own deployment response.
gaps.title: Incident response and advisory operation still need evidence

gaps.remediation: Write decision records through one record writer into a hash-chained local audit with signed heads, then add a command that exports them for assessors.
gaps.title: Gate decision records are not tamper-evident and cannot be exported

gaps.remediation: Authenticate every inbound request to the relay and allow only listed senders and channels, as planned for the relay.
gaps.title: The messaging relay has no inbound authentication yet

gaps.remediation: Attest the release artifacts with GitHub artifact attestations in the Release workflow, and verify them when the dashboard data is refreshed.
gaps.title: No build provenance or attestation for the VSIX, the relay image or the package

gaps.remediation: Build an SBOM of the relay image and scan it with a pinned, checksummed scanner, reporting high and critical findings.
gaps.title: No vulnerability scan or SBOM for the relay container image

gaps.remediation: Run static analysis on every pull request and on main, and keep its results as evidence.
gaps.title: No static analysis of the source code

gaps.remediation: Add a CODEOWNERS file that names the owner for the gate paths and the compliance sources.
gaps.title: No CODEOWNERS file; review routing is by convention

gaps.remediation: The hub's backup, restore and restore drill are documented; the relay's operator runbook adds its backups, restore and upgrades.
gaps.title: No backup and recovery guidance for the messaging relay

gaps.remediation: Publish one threat model and a data-flow diagram per component, each reviewed at least once a year.
gaps.title: No standalone threat model or data-flow diagram

gaps.remediation: Save exact versions for the root package, turn install scripts off where the build allows it, and turn on alerts for security updates only.
gaps.title: Root installs run dependency install scripts, development dependencies use ranges, and there are no automated update alerts

gaps.remediation: Document what each component logs, where and for how long, and give your organization an option to forward logs to its own monitoring; keeping and reviewing them is shared.
gaps.title: No central log forwarding or retention guidance

gaps.remediation: Make the docs check (and later the compliance check) required on main; the owner changes this repository setting, and the gap closes when the settings collector sees it.
gaps.title: The docs build is not a required check

gaps.remediation: Check the platform's TCB status, certificate revocation and the enclave's measurements against the provider's published build; until then the security policy says so and points to the provider's full verifier.
gaps.title: The attestation checks do not check TCB status, certificate revocation or enclave measurements

gaps.remediation: Give the three reserved compartments their fixed meaning through the exportControl section of the signed policy, with the words shown for each, and enforce it.
gaps.title: The CGP, ITAR and EAR compartments have no fixed meaning that ties them to a regime

gaps.remediation: Let only a signed export-person decision from the regime's official give a person a reserved compartment, and later issue those decisions as verifiable credentials.
gaps.title: Clearances are self-declared; there is no signed person decision for export regimes

gaps.remediation: Refuse every send of controlled content to an endpoint that no signed export-endpoint decision covers, in the route check.
gaps.title: Endpoints carry a highest label and a region, but no export eligibility

gaps.remediation: Refuse agent tools that reach the network while a chat holds a reserved compartment, and later add the full network fence around agent execution.
gaps.title: Agent network tools are refused only by the no-agent-tools flag, not by the marking

gaps.remediation: Write export-control records into the hash-chained audit and export them as a signed bundle for the officials.
gaps.title: Export-control records are not tamper-evident and cannot be exported

gaps.remediation: Never prune export-control records automatically, show the earliest date each may be pruned, and record a keyed hash of what was sent.
gaps.title: No retention rule, and no content hash in records, so a later marking cannot find earlier sends

gaps.remediation: Open an incident when controlled content may have reached an ineligible place, show the regulators' clocks, and notify your organization's export-control contact.
gaps.title: No incident flow for a possible release

gaps.remediation: Document the comparable-strength basis in the cryptography inventory, and evaluate a FIPS 140-3 validated provider for the hub and the appliance where the operating system can supply one; your organization decides whether the basis suffices.
gaps.title: The product's cryptography is not run as a FIPS 140 validated module

gaps.remediation: Ask about technical data for military or defence goods in setup, in plain words, with Not sure applying both markings, and add the export-control contact topic.
gaps.title: Setup asks nothing about export-controlled work, and there is no export-control contact topic

gaps.remediation: Check export decisions in hub grants and access lists, in the data platform's row access, and in the relay's channel manifests.
gaps.title: The hub, the data platform and the relay do not know export decisions

gaps.remediation: Add the requirement catalogues, their mappings and the two overlay pages to the Accreditation section.
gaps.title: No Controlled goods or ITAR overlay on the dashboard

gaps.remediation: Publish a Controlled goods and ITAR page that says what the product does, what it does not do, and the interim settings your officials may choose.
gaps.title: No published guidance for organizations on controlled goods and ITAR
